## English

FluentRead 0.0.42 adds optional local privacy checks for text translation, expands video subtitles and sentence learning, and improves image translation, scanned PDFs, and everyday reading controls.

### Webpage translation and controls

- Choose one-click toolbar translation to translate or restore the current page directly. This is opt-in; the quick panel remains the default toolbar action.
- In Chrome and Edge, choose whether the translation sidebar belongs to the current tab or the whole window. The current-tab setting is the default.
- Improved multi-paragraph Bilibili and AI translation fallback handling. Emoji and spacing at paragraph boundaries are preserved locally.
- Preserve GitHub user and repository names and native page controls. Selection translation stays available when the selection crosses decorative icons.
- Fixed input-translation restoration and cleanup when pages or panels reopen, so callbacks from closed interfaces do not affect the new view.

### Images and documents

- Choose CPU (WASM) for local PaddleOCR and LaMa processing, or keep automatic backend selection. Runtime details show the processing stage, initialized backend, and automatic CPU fallback.
- Improved image and manga text recognition, word spacing, wrapping, and placement. Background repair better preserves flat backgrounds, ruled lines, and nearby illustration details.
- After OCR, scanned PDF text can be selected and copied. Correct recognized source text or re-recognize the current page; uncertain numbers remain available for review against the original.
- PDF original-layout translations keep their line breaks and placement while zooming. Searchable exports preserve format characters and joined emoji sequences.
- Fixed batch-import progress, output selection, and ZIP controls in the document sidebar, including narrow-window layouts.

### Video subtitles and learning

- Added native caption timelines for Bilibili, Udemy (including Business), and edX, and support for embedded YouTube players.
- Float the full-sentence learning card out of a small player, drag it, adjust its height, and dock it back while retaining the current draft.
- Supported desktop browsers can choose the same local folder to reuse downloaded Whisper models. Existing complete models can be migrated to that folder.
- Improved handoff when YouTube caption tracks arrive early, and protected legitimate repeated captions from being removed.
- Bilingual SRT export uses a single timeline and handles overlapping cues.

### Privacy and translation services

- Added translation privacy protection under Advanced options, off by default. Choose local masking with restoration after translation, or block requests containing detected sensitive information.
- Configure detection categories and custom sensitive phrases. Rule-based detection can miss content; reading-assistant, AI-writing, audio-recognition, and cloud-OCR requests are outside this switch. See the [scope and controls](https://github.com/FluentRead/FluentRead/blob/v0.0.42/docs/en/config/privacy-protection.md).
- Image uploads through the translation interface are blocked while privacy protection is enabled; use local OCR followed by text translation instead.
- Added Mistral-hosted GLM and DeepSeek options to the model catalog. Unconfigured AI platforms are hidden by default, and restoring removed services from the custom-service dialog works again.

### Platform compatibility

- Improved Zotero's Windows dropdown keyboard controls and dismissal on outside input, Tab, or window focus loss.
- Google Drive's native authorization is offered only in confirmed desktop Google Chrome. Unsupported browsers receive clear guidance to use We

detail.readme:
# FluentRead **Closer languages. A bigger world.** An open-source browser extension for bilingual translation. [Install](#installation) · [Website](https://read.thinkstu.com/en/) · [User guide](https://read.thinkstu.com/en/guide/) · [Sponsorship](#sponsorship) · [Privacy policy](https://read.thinkstu.com/en/guide/privacy) · [简体中文](./misc/README_ZH.md) · [LINUX DO Community](https://linux.do) · [GPL-3.0](./LICENSE)
FluentRead displays translations alongside the original webpage and provides selection translation, AI reading assistance, image and document translation, and bilingual video subtitles. Its reading card provides contextual explanations and follow-up questions. We began developing FluentRead in January 2024. Since then, FluentRead has remained open source and free to use.
[![FluentRead introduction video](./docs/public/videos/fluentread-promo-en-poster.webp)](https://read.thinkstu.com/videos/fluentread-promo-en.mp4) [▶ Watch the 56-second introduction](https://read.thinkstu.com/videos/fluentread-promo-en.mp4) For a closer look, [watch the full official introduction (4+ minutes, in Chinese on Bilibili)](https://www.bilibili.com/video/BV1qhHJ6uEiF/).
## Features | Feature | Description | | --- | --- | | Webpage translation | Bilingual page translation, hover and selection translation, original-text restoration, and automatic translation rules. | | AI reading card | Meaning, sentence analysis, usage explanations, and practice, with paragraph context and follow-up questions. | | Learning center | Save words, phrases, and sentences with their original context for study and review. | | Image and area translation | Recognize text in webpage images or selected screen areas and display translations that can be copied. | | Document translation | Read PDF, ePub, DOCX, and other supported formats in two languages, edit translations, and export files. | | Video subtitles | Bilingual subtitles on YouTube and X, with original-only and translation-only display modes; supported X videos can also use local AI transcription. | | Services and settings | Free translation services, DeepL, AI providers, and local Ollama models, with glossaries, translation styles, shortcuts, and menu layout settings. | See the [user guide](https://read.thinkstu.com/en/guide/) for instructions and supported formats. AI explanations require a configured AI service. Third-party pricing and availability depend on the provider. ## Installation [Chrome](https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/djnlaiohfaaifbibleebjggkghlmcpcj) · [Edge](https://microsoftedge.microsoft.com/addons/detail/kakgmllfpjldjhcnkghpplmlbnmcoflp) · [Firefox](https://addons.mozilla.org/en-US/firefox/addon/%E6%B5%81%E7%95%85%E9%98%85%E8%AF%BB/) · [Userscript](https://greasyfork.org/en/scripts/482986) 1. Install the extension and refresh the webpage. 2. Open FluentRead and select a target language. The source language defaults to automatic detection and can also be selected manually. 3. Choose “Translate page.” Enable selection translation and other tools in settings as needed. Store updates may arrive at different times. The userscript provides core webpage translation features. See the [installation guide](https://read.thinkstu.com/en/guide/getting-started) for browser and feature availability. ## Sponsorship The project is currently funded mainly out of pocket, with a few hundred US dollars spent each month on maintenance. We believe FluentRead can make the world a little better. Thank you to [**bilibili Index-Translate**](https://index-translate.bilibili.com/) for becoming FluentRead’s first sponsor. [Become a sponsor](https://read.thinkstu.com/en/guide/support#sponsorship) · [Email us](mailto:a1914493943@gmail.com?subject=FluentRead%20sponsorship) · [Add on WeChat](https://read.thinkstu.com/support/wechat-contact.jpg) ## Local development Use the Node.js version in `.nvmrc` to match CI. Run pnpm through Corepack to use the version pinned in `package.json` even when your shell has an older global pnpm. ```sh nvm install corepack pnpm install --frozen-lockfile ``` - `corepack pnpm dev` starts local development. - `corepack pnpm zip` builds and packages the Chrome extension. [Other browsers](./docs/maintainers/releases.md#本地打包) · [Firefox source review](./scripts/amo/README.md) ## Contributing Report bugs and propose changes through [Issues](https://github.com/FluentRead/FluentRead/issues). Pull requests for code, documentation, interface translations, and [website adaptation](./docs/contributing/site-adaptation.md) are welcome. ## Support FluentRead is an open-source project whose continued development is made possible by the generous support of its community. Voluntary contributions are welcome through either service.

## Acknowledgments FluentRead grows alongside a vibrant open-source community. We are grateful to the following projects and their contributors for their openness and generosity: - [Read Frog](https://github.com/mengxi-ream/read-frog) - [KISS Translator](https://github.com/fishjar/kiss-translator) - [Duo Translator](https://github.com/linuxscreen/duo-translator) - [InfoLens](https://github.com/dqy08/InfoLens) — Smart Highlighting is inspired by its surprisal heatmap idea (Apache-2.0)



Thank you to everyone who has contributed to FluentRead, including the many we couldn't name here, and to every user for embracing a product that is still far from perfect. We hope to keep building together with you, and to bring a little more good into the world. ## License and privacy FluentRead is released under [GPL-3.0](./LICENSE). See [third-party notices](./public/third-party-notices/) for component attribution and licenses. Settings and learning records stay local by default; cloud translation uses your selected provider. Optional cloud configuration backup supports Google Drive and [WebDAV](https://read.thinkstu.com/en/guide/webdav), including service credentials while excluding wordbooks, conversations, and usage statistics. See the [privacy policy](https://read.thinkstu.com/en/guide/privacy) for permissions, encryption, and deletion details. ## Star History
